Experience.title: Experience
Experience.description: Represents an individual's documented experience using one or more radar items (tools, techniques) within a specific project context.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Experience entity.

title.description: A concise title summarizing the experience.

summary.description: A brief overview of the experience.

toolRadarItemIds.description: References to RadarItem entities that were used in this experience. (Relationship: Experience N:N RadarItem)

howUsed.description: Detailed description of how the tools were used, including workflows or steps.

promptsOrTemplates.description: Optional text area for prompts, code templates, or specific configurations used.

findings.description: Key findings, outcomes, what worked, what didn't work, and any surprises.

recommendations.description: Recommendations on when to use or when not to use the tools based on this experience.

roleTitle.description: The professional role of the user logging the experience (e.g., Strategist, Designer).

jobDescription.description: Optional detailed description of the user's job or responsibilities relevant to the experience.

teamDiscipline.description: The team or discipline associated with the experience (e.g., 'Creative', 'Development').

projectContext.description: Details about the project, such as client/internal, project type, or scope.

dataSensitivity.description: The sensitivity level of the data involved in the experience (e.g., 'Public', 'Internal', 'Client Confidential').

outcomeRating.description: A rating of the outcome of the experience, typically on a scale of 1 to 5.

timeSavedHours.description: Optional estimate of hours saved due to this experience or the tools used.

tags.description: A list of tags to categorize the experience.

links.description: An array of URLs to relevant documentation, examples, or assets.

status.description: The moderation status of the experience (e.g., 'Published' or 'Hidden').

viewsCount.description: The number of times this experience has been viewed.

likesCount.description: The number of likes this experience has received.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the experience was first created.

createdBy.description: Reference to the User who created this experience. (Relationship: User 1:N Experience)

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the experience was last updated.

updatedBy.description: Reference to the User who last updated this experience. (Relationship: User 1:N Experience)

ExperienceComment.title: ExperienceComment
ExperienceComment.description: Represents a comment associated with a specific user experience.

id.description: Unique identifier for the ExperienceComment entity.

experienceId.description: Reference to the Experience entity this comment belongs to. (Relationship: Experience 1:N ExperienceComment)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the comment was created.

createdBy.description: Reference to the User who created the comment. (Relationship: User 1:N ExperienceComment)

definition.description: Top-level collection for all Experience entries. Documents include `createdBy` for ownership, `status` for moderation (Published/Hidden), and `toolRadarItemIds` for linking to RadarItems. This structure ensures Authorization Independence by denormalizing authorization context directly into the document, avoiding `get()` calls in rules for ownership or status checks. Supports QAPs by allowing `list` queries filtered by `status == 'Published'` for authenticated users.

Subcollection for comments related to a specific Experience. Each comment document includes `createdBy` for ownership and `experienceId` for explicit linking to its parent. This provides Authorization Independence for comment-specific permissions and supports QAPs for listing comments for a given experience.

params.name: experienceId
params.description: The unique identifier of the Experience document to which the comments belong.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for Experiences prioritizes Authorization Independence and Query-After-Permissions (QAPs) by leveraging structural segregation and denormalization. The core principle is to avoid `get()` calls in security rules for authorization, minimizing complexity and improving debuggability.

1.  **`/experiences` Collection:** This top-level collection will store all `Experience` documents. Each `Experience` document includes essential authorization context directly within itself:
    *   `createdBy`: Stores the `uid` of the user who created the experience. This allows for direct ownership checks (`request.auth.uid == resource.data.createdBy`) without needing to fetch additional user data for individual document access.
    *   `status`: This field, with values like `Published` or `Hidden`, dictates the visibility and moderation state. It's directly queried in rules (`resource.data.status == 'Published'`) to control read access.
    *   **Authorization Independence:** By having `createdBy` and `status` directly on the `Experience` document, rules for read, update, and delete can be evaluated atomically. For Admin roles, an existence check on a global `/roles_admin/{uid}` collection is used, which is an accepted pattern for global roles and doesn't introduce hierarchical dependencies for specific *data* authorization. This design ensures that creating an experience or updating its fields (except `createdBy`, which is protected) does not require complex cross-document lookups.
    *   **QAPs (Query-After-Permissions):** The `/experiences` collection is designed to support secure `list` operations. Users can query this collection, for example, to find all experiences where `toolRadarItemIds` contains a specific `radarItemId`. The security rules will then filter results to only include documents where `status == 'Published'` (for non-admins) and where the user has appropriate permissions (owner for edit/delete). This allows the frontend to perform broad queries while the backend enforces fine-grained access, adhering to the QAP principle.

2.  **`/experiences/{experienceId}/comments` Subcollection:** This subcollection stores `ExperienceComment` documents, directly nested under their respective `Experience` parent document. Each comment document will include:
    *   `createdBy`: Stores the `uid` of the user who authored the comment, enabling direct ownership checks for modifying their own comments.
    *   `experienceId`: Redundantly stores the parent `Experience`'s ID. While implicitly part of the path, storing it directly can simplify certain index-based queries and data integrity checks.
    *   **Authorization Independence:** Comment authorization is independent of the parent `Experience`'s owner. A comment's owner can modify their comment, and read access to comments typically mirrors read access to the parent experience. This avoids `get()` calls to the parent `Experience` document for comment-specific permissions.
    *   **QAPs:** Listing comments for a specific experience (`/experiences/{experienceId}/comments`) is straightforward and secure, as read access for comments would typically be granted if the user has read access to the parent `Experience` (e.g., if the parent `Experience` is `Published`).

This structure ensures clear, explicit authorization rules, supports atomic operations, and facilitates efficient, secure list queries for all defined use cases.
